title: Endpoint-level usage & cost decomposition — console walkthrough
summary: Redwood AE+SE demoed the Console focusing on endpoint/endpoint-path usage analytics, per-endpoint dashboards, and cost decomposition. Customer asked about VPC/private deployment, KMS for keys, and how prefix caching and batching affect per-endpoint cost. Agreed next steps: pilot proposal, security docs, and a short benchmark run on a representative endpoint.
action_items: Maya: send pilot proposal + pricing sheet (due 2029-07-19)
Liam: share benchmark plan and a sample tracing hook config (due 2029-07-18)
Priya: provide list of top 10 endpoints and typical QPS/latency targets (due 2029-07-17)
next_steps: Redwood to run 1-week pilot with 2 endpoints (estimate and config)
Share SOC2 + ISO docs and private deployment checklist
Follow-up call next Tue to review pilot scope and timeline
transcript:
Meeting header: 2029-07-15 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~54m | Recording: enabled
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Jared (Aperture ML), Priya (Platform), Elena (Finance)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros — I'm Maya, I'm the AE on the account, and Liam is our SE who will run most of the demo.
[00:12] Jared: Hi all, Jared here. We're excited to see endpoint-level visibility — we have a lot of small endpoints with wildly different token profiles.
[00:20] Liam: Great, I'll share my screen. Just to set expectations: we'll focus on the Console — usage analytics, per-endpoint dashboards, and a cost breakdown down to path-level. We'll also show how caching and batching change the economics.
[00:33] Priya: Sounds good. For context we run a mix of hosted and private workloads, and we care about both month-end cost and latency SLOs.
[00:42] Elena: And finance will want a clean allocation per product line.
[00:47] Liam: Understood. Okay loading the Console... (screen share noises) you should see the Usage Overview landing page. The first panel is total token spend, broken into generation vs embeddings and then by model family.
[01:10] Liam: If we click into Endpoints -> you can see each endpoint listed and an aggregate cost column. We intentionally show cost normalized per 1k QPS and per 1M tokens so you can compare.
[01:23] Jared: Is that normalized for batching behavior or raw tokens?
[01:26] Liam: Good question — the normalization assumes baseline batching config set in Optimize. There's a toggle to switch between raw token cost (what happened) and normalized cost (what would happen with recommended batching).
[01:39] Priya: Do you recommend a single batching policy across endpoints? We have real-time chat endpoints and async summarization.
[01:46] Liam: Usually not. The Console can suggest per-endpoint batching/timeout values based on latency distributions. For chat we lean low batch sizes with prefix/K V cache engaged, for async we suggest higher batching.
[01:58] Jared: Can you show an example where batching changed cost but kept p95 under the SLO?
[02:03] Liam: Yep. Switching to endpoint "patient-note-summarizer" — here's the timeline. Before Optimize suggestions, average tokens per request were 1.2k, 95th latency ~420ms, cost per 1k reqs ~ $17. After enabling suggested batching (and LRU prefix cache for repeated prefixes) cost drops to $9 per 1k requests and p95 is 450ms — so slight bump but still within your SLO of 500ms.
[02:30] Elena: That delta is fine — finance will care about the change in absolute spend.
[02:35] Liam: Right; the Console always shows both baseline and post-optimization projections so you can see actual savings.
[02:43] Maya: One thing customers often ask — how do we attribute cost to product lines when a single endpoint serves multiple tenants?
[02:50] Liam: We support route tagging and can attach metadata to requests — user_tenant, product, feature_flag. The chargeback view allows slicing by those tags.
[03:00] Priya: Nice. How accurate is that when KV cache hits reduce token counts invisibly?
[03:06] Liam: We surface cache-hit-adjusted tokens: there are three columns — raw tokens, cache-adjusted tokens, and billable tokens. In many cases cache reduces effective compute but we still show the token-level delta so you can see where a cache is masking cost.
[03:22] Jared: Can Redwood run an internal benchmark to mimic our endpoint traffic? We need numbers we can trust before committing to Dedicated.
[03:30] Maya: Absolutely. Liam will propose a benchmark plan after this. It usually includes a small synthetic workload and a run on a representative infra profile.
[03:38] Liam: I'll add a tracing hook to capture KV cache hits and latency per call — that gives us a per-path breakdown.
[03:46] [04:00] (screen pause, switching dashboards)
[04:10] Liam: Now the per-endpoint dashboard. On the left the heatmap shows QPS by hour, center is cost by path, bottom is top prompt templates. You can click any cell and it surfaces the raw transcripts and prompt examples.
[04:26] Priya: That prompt examples section — is that stored? We have retention policies.
[04:30] Liam: Yes, by default it's redacted and hashed; raw prompts are only kept if you opt in for evals. We also integrate with customer KMS so logs can be encrypted at rest.
[04:42] Priya: KMS is important — can you confirm HSM support?
[04:45] Liam: Yes, for Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM. For hosted we offer bring-your-own-key options integrated with our managed KMS.
[04:55] Elena: And audit logs? Our auditors will want immutable logs for a 12-month window.
[04:59] Maya: We have an audit-log export feature and can configure retention; we'll share the compliance docs after this call.
[05:05] Jared: Cool. Back to costs — can we get a CSV export with per-path cost allocated to product codes?
[05:12] Liam: Yep, export shows per-path, per-tag, and you can map tags to GL codes before export.
[05:18] [06:00] (Liam navigates to Cost Decomposition view)
[06:08] Liam: This view breaks down cost by model instance, sequence length distribution, and pipeline steps (tokenization, generation, post-processing). You can see how quantization changes costs — we have sample profiles for int8 and awq-quant runs.
[06:25] Jared: Any degradation with int8 for our summarization model?
[06:28] Liam: In our tests summary quality delta was minor for the 7B family but you should run evals. Optimize will produce a recommended quantization profile per endpoint plus a quality regression alert if evals drift.
[06:40] Priya: How about canary rollouts? I want to shift 10% traffic to a cheaper model for a week and measure accuracy.
[06:46] Liam: Console supports canary policies per endpoint by percent and time window; you can auto rollback on error or on quality regression thresholds. We also surface side-by-side metrics for canary vs baseline.
[06:58] Elena: Do you charge for canary traffic differently?
[07:02] Liam: It's the same charge model; but the Console shows projected savings if the canary is cheaper.
[07:08] [07:45] (brief cross talk)
[07:50] Jared: Security question — in Private deployment mode does Redwood touch unencrypted prompts?
[07:55] Maya: For Private the control plane is customer-managed and prompt flows can be configured to never leave VPC. We can ensure end-to-end encryption; we'll send the specific architecture diagram.
[08:06] Priya: Great. Another technical detail — does the routing layer support region-aware fallback? We need EU-only routing for some endpoints.
[08:13] Liam: Yes, routing policies can be region-restricted and will failover to a permitted fallback region based on policy. We log the routing reason for each request.
[08:22] Jared: Could you show the per-request trace output?
[08:26] Liam: Sure — clicking a sample request shows timeline: ingress -> routing decision -> batch join -> KV cache lookup -> kernel exec -> response. Each stage has timestamps and resource counters. Note sometimes the transcript shows 'K V cache' spelled out in the trace which came up earlier in our logs—S O R T of transcription artifact.
[08:47] Priya: Haha, yeah transcription quirks.
[08:51] [09:30] (Liam scrolls)
[09:34] Liam: Here's a view of 'billable tokens' vs 'compute tokens' — you can see instances where billable tokens are higher (e.g., embeddings at fixed unit pricing) while compute tokens map to GPU time.
[09:45] Elena: That distinction is super helpful for finance — saves us from double-counting.
[09:50] Jared: On the topic of double-counting, what about retries — we have an aggressive retry policy in our client.
[09:56] Liam: Console has a retry-aware metric that collapses deduped retries and also shows raw counts so you can tune client-side.
[10:05] [10:40] Maya: Let's talk pilot scope. Jared, you mentioned two endpoints — which ones?
[10:46] Jared: The patient-note-summarizer and the intake-chat endpoint. Summarizer is high tokens/low QPS, chat is low tokens/high QPS.
[10:55] Liam: Perfect pair for testing both dimensions. We'll configure a pilot with tracing and Optimize recommendations enabled. Expect a 1-week run.
[11:05] Priya: Will the pilot require us to route traffic through Redwood? We prefer a shadow traffic mode first.
[11:10] Liam: Shadow mode is supported — you can mirror traffic and we return logs only, no production impact. For final numbers we often do a small percentage of live traffic.
[11:19] Priya: Okay good.
[11:22] [12:00] (short pause as Liam prepares the benchmark sheet)
[12:10] Liam: Sharing a spreadsheet now — it shows test plan, workload, metrics, and expected outputs. I also put a tracing hook snippet for our SDK.
[12:22] Jared: Do you need any credentials?
[12:25] Maya: We'll need a read-only S3 bucket for log export and an endpoint to mirror. We'll include instructions in the pilot email.
[12:33] Elena: Regarding procurement — we usually need a 3-month contracted commitment for Reserved/Dedicated. Is there flexibility?
[12:40] Maya: There's some flexibility — we typically start with a pilot on hosted, then if the numbers are good we discuss Dedicated sizing and term. We can do a month-to-month reserved pool as a bridge in some cases.
[12:52] Elena: OK I'll flag that.
[12:55] [13:30] (Liam navigates to Alerts & Cost Budgets)
[13:34] Liam: Here you can create budgets per-product line and get Slack/email alerts when spend deviates. There's also anomaly detection for sudden spike in tokens or latency regressions.
[13:45] Priya: Is anomaly detection self-tuning? We have seasonal spikes around release windows.
[13:50] Liam: It has adaptive baselining and you can pin expected seasonality windows. We also let you annotate windows so future detection ignores planned spikes.
[14:02] Jared: Can we map these alerts to PagerDuty?
[14:05] Liam: Yep, integrations include PagerDuty, Opsgenie, Slack, and webhooks.
[14:11] [15:00] (brief interjection from Maya)
[15:06] Maya: A quick note on price transparency — Console will also show per-token unit cost per model and historical changes if you switch model variants.
[15:15] Elena: That's useful when we're evaluating cheaper model variants.
[15:19] [16:00] (Liam demonstrates a cost scenario builder)
[16:07] Liam: In Cost Scenario Builder you can simulate replacing a model with a quantized variant, or enabling a cache, and it will project monthly spend.
[16:18] Priya: Any hidden infra costs to consider for Private? GPUs, network egress?
[16:22] Liam: Private deployments will include infra estimators — egress is shown in the export. For Dedicated we provide recommended instance families; you manage the infra or we can do a managed config.
[16:33] Jared: For our compliance team, they want a list of supported certifications and a network diagram.
[16:38] Maya: We'll attach SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001 artifacts and a Private deployment network diagram in the follow-up email.
[16:45] Elena: Great.
[17:00] [18:00] (Liam shows a deep-dive into a high-cost path)
[18:08] Liam: This path is expensive because of repeated long context windows from connector ingestion. The Console flags these top-k prompt templates and suggests truncation or caching of static context.
[18:21] Priya: Truncation might reduce quality. Do you have a soft-truncation suggestion?
[18:26] Liam: We provide a heuristics library — e.g., keep last N utterances plus a hashed summary block. Optimize can generate the summary block and you'd pay for the summary cost but save on repeated context.
[18:38] Jared: Any telemetry on how customers typically split that cost?
[18:42] Liam: Many customers shift summary generation to an async job and attach a compact summary to the request; others store summaries in KV cache keyed by conversation id.
[18:52] [20:00] (discussion continues, slight interruptions, some transcribed mis-hearings: 'awq' sometimes as 'a w q')
[20:10] Priya: Can we run an eval to make sure the summary approach doesn't regress clinical safety intents?
[20:15] Liam: Yes, we can hook into your eval harness and run diff metrics; Optimize will flag any regression above your threshold.
[20:25] Jared: What's the turnaround for pilot results?
[20:28] Maya: Typically 7-10 business days after the end of the pilot to analyze and present findings.
[20:34] Elena: Perfect. 
[20:40] [22:00] (Liam scrolls to Billing exports)
[22:05] Liam: Example CSV has columns: timestamp, endpoint_id, path_tag, raw_tokens, cache_adjusted_tokens, billable_tokens, model_variant, region, cost_usd, gl_code. You can map gl_code before ingesting to your accounting systems.
[22:19] Priya: Will the mapping be automated?
[22:22] Liam: Yes, we have a mapping config file you can manage in the Console; it will persist per workspace.
[22:30] [25:00] (short silence while notes typed)
[25:20] Maya: Before we wrap, any blockers from your side?
[25:25] Jared: We need SOC2 docs and a short benchmark plan. Priya will need the tracing hook. Elena wants an indicative cost for a 90-day pilot on hosted vs dedicated.
[25:38] Maya: We'll take those. Liam will own the benchmark plan and the tracing hook, I'll own pricing/pilot paperwork and procurement notes.
[25:48] Priya: One last question — do you have any customers in regulated healthcare we can talk to?
[25:53] Maya: We do a reference that can be arranged under NDA; we'll include potential refs in the follow-up.
[26:00] [26:45] (closing remarks and casual small talk)
[27:05] Liam: I'll ping the pilot spreadsheet in the chat and include the tracing snippet.
[27:12] Maya: We'll send the security bundle and sample contract.
[27:18] Elena: Thanks, that was helpful.
[27:22] Jared: Thanks everyone.
[27:25] Maya: Alright wrapping up — next call proposed Tuesday 2029-07-23 to finalize the pilot scope.
[27:33] Priya: Works for me.
[27:36] [53:40] (end of recorded transcript; some sections elided for brevity)

NOTES: transcript includes occasional mis-hearings and auto-captions (e.g., 'a w q' for AWQ quant, 'K V cache' tokenization). Shared artifacts: pilot plan spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.internal/pilots/aperture-2029), security bundle (link: https://redwood.internal/security/aperture-bundle).
